briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The declared temporary ceasefire between the US and Iran is highly unstable, immediately challenged by extensive Israeli military operations against Hezbollah across Lebanon, resulting in significant Lebanese casualties and widespread international condemnation. Concurrently, Iran has asserted new controls over the Strait of Hormuz, leading to disrupted shipping and increased oil prices, while both sides prepare for potential renewed conflict should diplomatic efforts fail.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran are currently under a temporary two-week ceasefire with the US, though this is contested by Iran regarding its scope. Mojtaba Khamenei, identified as the new Leader, issued a written message marking the 40th day of the late Leader's martyrdom, asserting that Iran will seek reparations for war damages, will not renounce its rights, and will manage the Strait of Hormuz in a "new phase." Press TV indicated he stressed "continued public participation in the battle against US and Israeli aggression." Explosions and air defense activity were reported in Tehran, Karaj (Mahrshahr, Goudardasht), Tabriz, Mahabad, Ahvaz, and Shiraz, attributed to unidentified drones. The IRGC Ground Force commander stated Iran's geography is a "quagmire" for invaders. Iran-linked hackers, "Handala," claimed to have breached former IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi's phone, leaking photos and videos, including secret coordination with Jordan.

Internally, Iran reported over 3,000 fatalities with 40% unidentifiable, according to the head of the Medical Examiner's Organization, Abbas Masjedi. Mass mourning ceremonies for the late Leader Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei were held across Iran, including Isfahan and Tehran. Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, the Parliament Speaker, stated Iran's "10-point plan" for ceasefire requires an end to attacks on Lebanon and rejected negotiating under Trump's "ultimatum." Mohammad Eslami, head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization, dismissed calls to limit Iran's enrichment program as "mere wishes." Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that if the US allows Netanyahu to "kill diplomacy," Iran is "prepared" for the economic consequences.

Economically, Iran has proposed that fees for passage through the Strait of Hormuz be paid in cryptocurrency. Maritime tracking data from Kpler indicates no oil tankers have transited the Strait since the ceasefire, and only four non-Iranian vessels carrying dry cargo passed yesterday, according to the Wall Street Journal, causing oil prices to surge above $100 per barrel. The IRGC Navy announced new alternate shipping routes (from March 9 to April 8) due to potential mines in the main traffic zone. TASS reported Iran will allow no more than 15 ships per day.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations are heavily focused on Lebanon, with Prime Minister Netanyahu explicitly stating, "There is no ceasefire in Lebanon. We continue to strike Hezbollah with great force, and we will not stop until we restore security." IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir toured Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon, declaring it "our main combat arena" and approving new battle plans. The IDF launched extensive airstrikes against Hezbollah rocket launching sites, killing over 200 Hezbollah operatives in "Operation Eternal Darkness" yesterday, bringing the total in this campaign to over 1,400. Key figures killed include Ali Yusuf Harshi, personal secretary and nephew of Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem, in Beirut's Tallet Khayat neighborhood, and Maher Qassem Hamdan, commander of the Hezbollah-allied Lebanese Resistance Companies in the Shebaa area, along with eight other operatives in Sidon. The IDF also struck two "central" Litani River crossings and approximately 10 weapon depots, rocket launchers, and Hezbollah headquarters in southern Lebanon.

On the home front, northern Israel experienced significant rocket fire from Lebanon, with sirens sounding in Haifa, Acre, Nahariya, Metulla, Kiryat Shmona, Misgav Am, Avivim, Margaliot, Manara, Even Menachem, Zarit, Netua, Fassuta, Shomera, Shtula, Abirim, Maona, Mi'ilya, Ma'a lot Tarshicha, Gornot HaGalil, and Shlomi. Hostile aircraft intrusions were detected in the Western Galilee and Nahariya area. The IDF reported approximately 70 rockets fired from Lebanon today, with 15 targeting Nahariya and surrounding areas, resulting in two lightly injured civilians. No reports of injuries from rockets in Haifa or Kiryat Shmona. Home Front Command guidelines remain unchanged until Friday, April 10, 2026, at 17:00. The IDF warned of possible rocket fire towards "additional areas in the State of Israel" in the coming hours.

Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu announced that he instructed his cabinet to begin direct negotiations with Lebanon "as soon as possible," focusing on disarming Hezbollah and establishing peaceful relations. This decision was reportedly made at the request of US President Trump, who asked Netanyahu to reduce attacks in Lebanon to aid negotiations with Iran. A senior Israeli official indicated that the Israeli Ambassador to the US would lead talks with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun. Defense Minister Israel Katz detailed a new "security zone" in southern Lebanon, comprising four lines (border, defensive, anti-tank, Litani River), and stated the IDF would strike from the air "with great force." The Israeli cabinet also secretly approved 34 new West Bank settlements. In a security briefing, Boaz Bismut, head of Israel's Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, stated there is a "possibility the campaign will resume in the coming days."

A 17-year-old pedestrian was seriously injured in Safed after being hit by a motorcycle. Public opinion polls published after the ceasefire show 51-53% of the public oppose the cessation of fighting against Iran, while 79% support continued attacks against Hezbollah.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces killed Abd al-Rahman Ammar Hassan Khudari, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad operative who participated in the October 7, 2023, attack on Kibbutz Nir Oz and was planning an attack on Israeli troops in northern Gaza. Muhammad Washah, a "key" Hamas operative and Al Jazeera journalist involved in rocket and weapons production and planning attacks, was also killed in the central Gaza Strip. The IDF reported responding to a stone-throwing incident near the village of Taysir, resulting in injuries to an Israeli civilian and a Palestinian. Israel Hayom reported that Israel is preparing for renewed military operations in Gaza as Hamas's deadline to disarm expires today, with Hamas sources indicating a refusal is likely. Press TV reported the death of 9-year-old Ritaj Rehan in her classroom in Gaza by an Israeli sniper.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations included firing approximately 70 rockets from Lebanon toward northern Israel today, with barrages targeting Haifa, Nahariya, Kiryat Shmona, Metulla, and other border communities. Hezbollah claimed clashes with Israeli soldiers in Bint Jbeil, using light arms and RPG fire. The IDF stated that Hezbollah has fired approximately 3,000 rockets and projectiles from areas south of the Litani River since March 2, asserting this proves the Lebanese army "lied" about dismantling Hezbollah's infrastructure.

Israeli strikes were extensive, with the Lebanese Ministry of Health reporting at least 303 fatalities in Israeli attacks yesterday. The Lebanese Army also announced four soldiers were killed. Defense Minister Israel Katz stated over 200 Hezbollah operatives were killed yesterday in "Operation Eternal Darkness," bringing the campaign's total to over 1,400. Israeli airstrikes targeted Hezbollah rocket launching sites, two "central" Litani River crossings used for weapons transfers, and approximately 10 weapon depots, rocket launchers, and Hezbollah headquarters in southern Lebanon. An evacuation warning was issued for Beirut's southern suburbs (Dahiyeh), leading to massive congestion as residents fled. The Lebanese poet Khatoun Salma and her husband were reportedly killed in Israeli bombardments in Beirut.

Regarding negotiations, Lebanese official sources state that a direct dialogue with Israel, mediated by the US, is expected to begin next week in Washington, with former Ambassador Simon Karam leading the Lebanese delegation. However, Lebanon's official stance is to secure a ceasefire *before* entering negotiations. Prime Minister Nawaf Salam proposed declaring Beirut a "demilitarized city" and will file an urgent UN Security Council complaint over Israeli attacks.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Iraq, the US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State summoned the Iraqi ambassador to condemn militia attacks on US diplomatic facilities and personnel, emphasizing that Baghdad's failure to prevent such attacks negatively affects bilateral relations. Explosions were reported in Basra and Erbil. Kuwait's Ministry of Defense stated that drone attacks on its vital facilities appeared to originate from Iraqi territory. Kata'ib Hezbollah in Iraq reported 25 of its members, including senior commanders, were killed in fighting over the last month.

GULF STATES
Kuwait reported extensive damage to its National Guard building due to a drone attack, with no casualties, and later announced it was facing missile and drone attacks targeting vital facilities. The Kuwaiti Foreign Ministry condemned Iran and its proxies, including armed factions and militias, for these attacks.

Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy reported attacks on several energy sites, including the Manifa production facility and the Khurais facility, leading to a reduction of approximately 700,000 barrels per day in oil production. One Saudi worker was killed and seven injured. This statement from the Energy Ministry was noted as contradicting earlier claims from the Saudi Defense Ministry regarding successful interceptions.

The UAE Ministry of Defense stated no Iranian cruise missiles, ballistic missiles, or drones were detected in its airspace on April 9. However, the CEO of ADNOC (Abu Dhabi National Oil Company), Sultan Al Jaber, affirmed that the Strait of Hormuz must be open unconditionally, adding that any vessel passage through the Strait requires Iran's permission. US diplomatic sources told CBS that Iran proposed paying passage fees for the Strait of Hormuz in cryptocurrencies, which was refused by the US.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Fragile US-Iran Ceasefire:** A temporary two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran is in effect, but its stability and scope are highly contested. Iranian leaders (Mojtaba Khamenei, Qalibaf, Pezeshkian) maintain that ongoing Israeli attacks on Lebanon constitute a violation, making further diplomatic progress conditional on their cessation.
2.  **Intensified Israeli Operations in Lebanon:** Israel launched extensive airstrikes across Lebanon, killing over 200 Hezbollah operatives in "Operation Eternal Darkness" yesterday, including Ali Yusuf Harshi (nephew and personal secretary of Naim Qassem) and Maher Qassem Hamdan (commander of Lebanese Resistance Companies). Lebanese officials reported 303 fatalities from Israeli strikes yesterday, including four Lebanese Army soldiers.
3.  **Strait of Hormuz Disruptions:** Iran's new Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, asserted a "new phase" of management for the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC Navy announced temporary alternate shipping routes due to potential mines. Maritime data indicates no oil tankers have transited the Strait since the ceasefire, causing global oil prices to rise above $100 per barrel.
4.  **Israeli-Lebanese Negotiation Initiative:** Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu announced the initiation of direct negotiations with Lebanon to disarm Hezbollah and establish peace, reportedly at the request of US President Trump, who urged a reduction in Israeli strikes in Lebanon to facilitate Iran talks. Lebanon, however, insists on a ceasefire *before* talks begin.
5.  **Iranian Domestic Impact and Casualties:** Over 3,000 Iranians have been killed in the war, with 40% of bodies unidentifiable, according to Iran's Medical Examiner. Explosions were reported in multiple Iranian cities (Tehran, Karaj, Tabriz, Mahabad, Ahvaz, Shiraz), attributed to air defense activity against unidentified drones.
6.  **Saudi Energy Infrastructure Attacks:** Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy reported significant attacks on key oil facilities (Manifa, Khurais) leading to a reduction of 700,000 barrels per day in oil production, and one fatality with seven injuries.
7.  **Iranian Nuclear Stance:** Mohammad Eslami, head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization, publicly rejected any demands to limit Iran's uranium enrichment program, stating such "wishes" would "go to the grave."

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain critically high due to conflicting interpretations of the ceasefire's scope, particularly concerning Lebanon. Israel's determined continuation and intensification of military operations against Hezbollah in Lebanon, coupled with Prime Minister Netanyahu's explicit denial of a ceasefire in that arena, directly contradicts Iran's and its allies' position that Lebanon is an "inseparable part" of the ceasefire. This creates an immediate flashpoint that could derail diplomatic efforts and trigger Iranian retaliation.

The Strait of Hormuz is an active flashpoint; Iran's assertion of new management and reported disruptions to oil tanker traffic, combined with US warnings against charging fees, carry a high risk of naval confrontation or further economic warfare. Iran's nuclear chief's rejection of limiting enrichment also suggests potential for a breakdown in any broader peace talks.

Military posture changes include the IDF Chief of Staff approving new battle plans for Lebanon and Israel detailing a four-line "security zone" aimed at neutralizing Hezbollah. US President Trump's statements about keeping US forces "in and around Iran" and "looking forward to its next conquest" indicate readiness for renewed conflict if a deal is not reached. Iran, through figures like Qalibaf, has also warned of "strong responses" to ceasefire violations. The potential for Hamas to refuse disarmament in Gaza could also lead to renewed Israeli military operations there.

Red lines are actively being tested: Iran considers Israeli actions in Lebanon, alleged airspace violations (like a drone shot down in Fars province), and any attempt to deny its right to enrichment as breaches of its "10-point plan." The US and its allies consider unimpeded freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz a red line.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** has shown mixed signals. President Trump expressed optimism for a peace deal with Iran but warned of "very painful" consequences if no deal is reached. He also reportedly asked Prime Minister Netanyahu to reduce strikes in Lebanon to aid the Iran negotiations. Trump pressured European allies to provide "concrete military support," including warships, for securing the Strait of Hormuz and is reportedly considering withdrawing some US troops from Europe. The US also summoned Iraq's ambassador to condemn militia attacks on American diplomatic facilities.

**Pakistan** is actively mediating the US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad, with a delegation including Parliament Speaker Qalibaf and Foreign Minister Araghchi expected to arrive. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reportedly affirmed Lebanon's inclusion in the ceasefire agreement. However, Pakistan's Defense Minister, Khawaja Asif, strongly condemned Israel's actions in Lebanon, calling it "genocide" and Israel a "curse on humanity," drawing a rebuke from Israel's Prime Minister's Office.

**European Union members** have largely condemned Israel's intensified actions in Lebanon. **Spain** reopened its embassy in Tehran, with Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares accusing Israel of violating the ceasefire and international law with "hundreds of bombs" on Lebanon. **France's** Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot condemned Israeli attacks as "unacceptable" and called for Lebanon's inclusion in the ceasefire. **Belgium's** Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot reported narrowly escaping Israeli strikes in Beirut. **The UK's** Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper also stressed that Lebanon must be included in any ceasefire agreement. **Germany's** Chancellor Friedrich Merz expressed concern over Israel's conduct in Lebanon and requested an end to "increased attacks."

**Russia** announced an Easter ceasefire in Ukraine. Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov condemned Israeli attacks in Lebanon, stating they "jeopardize the negotiation process" and urged an immediate ceasefire and a political-diplomatic resolution.

**China**, through its Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ming, called for Lebanon's inclusion in the ceasefire. A UN Special Envoy for the Middle East, Jean Arnault, met with Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister to discuss the crisis.

**Turkey's** Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan warned against Israeli "sabotage" of the negotiations and expressed hope that the ceasefire would include Lebanon and become permanent. President Erdogan and Iranian President Pezeshkian discussed ceasefire efforts and regional security.

**Canada's** Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemned Israeli attacks in Lebanon.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist within the intelligence feed. The most significant contradiction surrounds the **scope of the US-Iran ceasefire**: Iranian, Pakistani, and several European sources explicitly state or imply that the ceasefire agreement includes a cessation of hostilities in Lebanon. Conversely, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu unequivocally denies any ceasefire in Lebanon, vowing to continue operations against Hezbollah. US statements are mixed, with Trump reportedly asking Netanyahu to reduce strikes in Lebanon, yet the US government's official text of any ceasefire remains unreleased and undefined in the provided messages.

**Casualty figures for Iran** are also inconsistent: Iran's Medical Examiner reported over 3,000 fatalities, while an unverified source (omid dana) claims over 10,000, and Al Jazeera cited 2,076.

**The status of Iran's leadership** post-Ali Khamenei's death is suggested as Mojtaba Khamenei by Press TV and Vahid Online, with omid dana making an unverified and highly inflammatory claim about the killing of Alireza Arafi to secure Mojtaba's leadership.

**Strait of Hormuz traffic** reports conflict: Kpler (via NBC) states no oil tankers have passed since the ceasefire, while the Wall Street Journal reported four non-Iranian dry cargo ships transited. The IRGC Navy's announcement of new routes implies some expectation of traffic.

**Propaganda indicators** are prevalent from multiple actors. Iranian sources consistently frame the situation as Iran's "victory" and "imposition of will," with leaders using strong, uncompromising language. The Pakistani Defense Minister's rhetoric against Israel is highly inflammatory, aligning with Iranian narratives. Israeli Defense Minister Katz's statement that Hezbollah is "pleading for a ceasefire" appears intended to project strength. Trump's "America is back!" and "next conquest" comments are typical of his populist style.

**Unverified claims** include 70 US transport planes arriving in the Middle East (omid dana), North Korea distancing itself from Iran (omid dana), and a Brazilian analyst's estimate of Iran possessing over 17,000 missiles. There is also an unconfirmed report of a hacker claiming to breach China's National Supercomputing Center.

**Reporting gaps** exist regarding the precise details and official texts of both the US-Iran ceasefire agreement and Iran's "10-point plan" versus the alleged US "15-point plan." The specific "US-Israeli attack" that killed Kamal Kharrazi is not fully detailed. The exact nature and targets of the alleged explosions in Iranian cities remain unconfirmed beyond air defense activity. Humanitarian conditions in Gaza receive limited attention in this feed, primarily focusing on specific military actions and civilian casualties.
